description:
Programme Overview

We are inviting applications for a fully funded PhD position in Petr Tesina's Research Group at CEITEC (Central European Institute of Technology), Masaryk University in Brno, Czechia — a leading European centre for life sciences with state-of-the-art research infrastructure. The PhD project centers on a fundamental question in molecular biology: How is human translation controlled at the structural level?

Research Focus

You will investigate the structures of ribosomal complexes involved in eukaryotic translation control, at the interface of structural biology, biochemistry, and molecular biology. The lab has recently secured substantial third-party funding — including an ERC Starting Grant and an EMBO Installation Grant — so your research and training will be well supported for years to come.

Training and Skills

  • Access to state-of-the-art cryo-EM instruments at our local core facility.
  • Comprehensive cryo-EM training provided — no prior cryo-EM experience required.
  • Hands-on experience with advanced techniques including CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, protein and RNA biochemistry, and biophysics methods.
  • Soft skills development in scientific communication, collaboration, and project management.

Funding and Benefits

  • Competitive ERC-funded salary starting at 30,000 CZK net, with yearly increase.
  • 6 weeks of paid holiday.
  • Medical insurance.
  • Meal and pension contributions.
  • Multisport card.
  • Mental health care.
  • Sports lessons directly on campus.
  • Kindergarten close to the campus.
  • Welcome Office support with visa and relocation assistance.
  • Flexible working hours.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Must-have: MSc or equivalent degree (preferably in Life Sciences), strong interest in structural biology, strong spoken and written English.
  • Nice-to-have: Hands-on experience with structural biology, biochemistry, or molecular biology methods; programming skills; experience with human or yeast cell cultures.
  • A background in structural biology and translation is the ultimate fit — but above all, we value curiosity, dedication, and a collaborative mindset.

Application Process

Submit your CV, motivation letter, list of publications, and contacts for at least two references via the e-application portal. Applications are open until 8 January 2027, but apply as soon as possible, as this is a rolling review and candidates are assessed in the order applications are received.

Official Links

  • Vacancy Page: https://www.muni.cz/en/about-us/careers/vacancies/81701
  • Lab Page: https://www.ceitec.eu/translation-control/rg396

Contact

Lenka Divinová (HR): lenka.divinova@ceitec.muni.cz

Important Notes

  • Rolling review — candidates assessed in order applications are received.
  • CEITEC MU offers flexible working hours, Welcome Office support, Grant Office backing, and a vibrant calendar of workshops and conferences.
  • As a PhD student in an EMBO Young Investigator lab, you gain direct access to exclusive international travel and exchange grants.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 8 January 2027. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
